content.title: Phillies vs. Rockies: Prediction, Lineups, How to Watch (4/3/26)
content.text: The Philadelphia Phillies (3–3) visit the Colorado Rockies (2–4) today at Coors Field to kick off a three-game set. The Phillies head on the road for the first time this season after a 3–3 homestand that ended on a high note with a comeback extra-inning win over the Washington Nationals in a toughly-contested series. Justin Crawford hit a game-winning RBI single in the bottom of the 10th, driving in Brandon Marsh, to secure the win. Cristopher Sanchez had another strong start for the Phillies, allowing just one run and four hits over 5.1 innings, striking out seven, while Cade Cavalli was just as strong for the other side. Both bullpens, however, let the floodgates open. Down 5-3 in the bottom of the ninth, Edmundo Sosa tied the game with a bases-loaded single, pushing the game into extra innings. Colorado, meanwhile, enters after defeating the Toronto Blue Jays 2–1 on Wednesday, powered by a strong start from Kyle Freeland and late offense. Freeland allows just one run and five hits over five innings, striking out six. Aaron Nola for Philadelphia against Michael Lorenzen for Colorado. Nola will look to settle in after allowing two home runs in his season debut while striking out seven. Lorenzen makes his home debut for the Rockies after a short first outing, lasting just 4.1 innings, allowing three runs and seven hits. Coors Field is likely to amplify offense, so expect this game to turn into a higher-scoring matchup. Philadelphia’s deeper lineup and edge in starting pitching may allow the Phillies to control the game late.
